payload.title: Aleph integrity workflow silently disables itself when yq is unavailable
payload.body: The new gate treats missing `yq` as `enabled=false`, so the downstream integrity job is skipped instead of failing closed. On a runner image without `yq`, or after runner image changes, a repository with `aleph.enabled: true` will still bypass `verify`, removing the workflow that authenticates the vendored Aleph bundle. The trigger is this diff-touched gate: `if command -v yq ...; then ...; fi`, followed by `if: needs.gate.outputs.enabled == 'true'`. Install/pin `yq` in the gate or parse the small YAML key with an action/tool already guaranteed by the workflow, and fail the gate on parser absence when `.loa.config.yaml` exists.

payload.title: Aleph release sync can be bypassed by parser absence in the opt-in gate
payload.body: The release-sync gate has the same fail-open behavior: if `yq` is missing, unreadable, or changes syntax, `enabled` remains `false` and both `prepare` and `propose` are skipped. For an opted-in repo, that suppresses the verify-and-seal path for a third-party vendored component without surfacing a failure. Because this workflow is security-sensitive release automation, parser absence should be a hard failure when the config file exists, not a no-op.
